newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins unchanged, watch U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins unchanged, watch U.S. data.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds remained virtually unchanged on Thursday in thin trade as morning gains after the London Club debt reconcilation figure were offset by profit-taking later, dealers said.
They said the market was waiting for U.S. second quarter gross domestic product figures on Thursday and July non-farm payrolls on Friday.
"There's been a little profit-taking just because Russia has had a rally on the back of the announcement yesterday of the 60 percent fully reconciled, " said Morgan Stanley Vice President Eric Fine.
On Wednesday a senior Finance Ministry official said the volume of fully reconciled Russian debt to the London Club of commercial creditors was about 60 percent.
The announcement indicated that the restructuring agreement signing, which will create the world's biggest single Brady bond, was one step nearer. The emerging debt market surged on the news.
Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said the market would very much depend on the U.S. GDP figure.

"The GDP is expected to be favourable for investors," Kovzharov said. "But if it is more than two percent, there may appear a wish to start profit-taking as we are now at world records. There have never been such prices or spreads (over U.S. Treasuries)."

Higher than expected GDP would spark fear among investors that the U.S. Federal Reserve would tighten interest rates, prompting sales of U.S. Treasuries. All dollar-denominated paper would follow and MinFin bonds would suffer most as the market was illiquid, Kovzharov said.
Analysts had forecast the rise in the GDP would be 1.9 percent.
The market is ignoring the political row around the sale of Svyazinvest telecoms holding, dealers said.
Kovzharov forecast a quiet market with a slight downward trend in the next month.
"Most likely we shall enter a summer lull," he said. "The market will be consolidating with a downward trend."
